changes: original_meaning 保留「光学」，并点明中世纪拉丁语原短语 perspectiva ars 的构词（perspicere 透过看）。
semantic_path 按 Etymonline 编年重建三站（光学 → 1590 年代透视画法 → 1762 年观点），how 逐站写明。
evidence: Etymonline: "perspective (n.) late 14c., perspectif, \"the science of optics,\"... from Medieval Latin perspectiva ars \"science of optics,\" from... Latin perspectus \"clearly perceived,\" past participle of perspicere \"inspect, look through, look closely at,\" from per \"through\" + specere \"look at\""

Etymonline: "The sense of \"the art of drawing solid objects on a flat surface so as to give appearance of distance or depth\" is attested by 1590s, probably by influence of Italian prospettiva... The meaning \"proper or just proportion, appropriate relation in the mind of the parts of a subject to one another\" is recorded by c. 1600, hence the figurative meaning \"mental outlook over time\" (1762)."
perspective.mechanism_sentence: perspective 是拉丁语「透过看」（per- 穿过 + specere 看）：中世纪它是一门研究看的科学——光学；后来成了画家在平面上造纵深的透视法，再借进脑子里，成了「观点」。

semantic_path.how: 研究『看』的科学落到了画布上：受意大利艺术术语 prospettiva 影响，1590 年代 perspective 添『在平面上画出远近纵深的技法』义——词库『透视』即此站。
画里的比例借进了心里（比喻）：约 1600 年先有『心中对各部分比例的恰当感』义，1762 年定型为『看事情的眼光与心态』——词库今义『视角；观点』即此。

evidence: Etymonline: "phenomenon (n.) 1570s, \"a fact directly observed, a thing that appears or is perceived, an occurrence,"... from Greek phainomenon \"that which appears or is seen,\" noun use of neuter present participle of phainesthai \"to appear,\" passive of phainein \"bring to light, cause to appear, show\""
Etymonline: "Meaning \"extraordinary occurrence\" is recorded by 1771. In philosophy, \"an appearance or immediate object of experience\" (1788)."
phenomenon.mechanism_sentence: phenomenon 是希腊语「显现出来的东西」（phainein 是「使显现、照亮」）：1570 年代入英语作可观察的「现象」，1771 年起也管非同寻常的奇人奇事。
phenomenon.original_meaning: 显现出来被看见的东西

semantic_path.meaning: 显现出来被看见的东西

semantic_path.how: 1570 年代入英语，被自然哲学收作术语：指『直接观察到的事实、出现的事物』——词库今义『现象』即此；1788 年哲学里又专指『经验的直接对象』。
出了格的现象另起炉灶：1771 年 phenomenon 添『非同寻常的发生』义，后来连了不起的人也叫 phenomenon——同一个词，从实验室的记录变成了惊叹号。

changes: original_meaning 按古英语 pinn 的 gloss 收为「栓，销钉」。
semantic_path 按 Etymonline 编年重建三站（粗栓 → 14 世纪末细钢丝大头针 → 1570 年代球瓶），how 写明物件变细的过程。
evidence: Etymonline: "pin (n.) late Old English pinn \"peg or bolt of wood or metal used to hold things in place or fasten them together\""

Etymonline: "The modern slender wire pin, used as a fastener for clothing or in sewing, is attested by this name by late 14c., perhaps late 13c.... The meaning \"wooden stick or club set up to be knocked down in a game\" (skittles, bowling, etc.) is by 1570s."
pin.mechanism_sentence: pin 在古英语里是一根木头或金属做的栓，管把东西固定住：14 世纪末，栓变细成了缝衣的大头针；1570 年代，立着挨打的保龄球瓶也借了这个名字。

semantic_path.how: 物件变细，名字留任：14 世纪末，pin 落到缝衣、别布用的细钢丝针上——从粗木栓到一根针，靠的是同一种功能：把东西别住、固定住。词库今义『别针；大头针』即此。
形状相认：1570 年代 pin 添游戏义，指立在场上等着被球打倒的木瓶（保龄球瓶）——一根粗短的『栓』立在那儿，名字顺手被借走。

evidence: Etymonline: "pine (n.) \"coniferous tree, tree of the genus Pinus,\" Old English pin (in compounds), from Old French pin and directly from Latin pinus \"pine, pine-tree, fir-tree,\" which is perhaps from a PIE *pi-nu-, from root *peie- \"to be fat, swell\"... If so, the tree's name would be a reference to its sap or pitch."
Etymonline: "The native Old English word was furh (see fir)."
Oxford: "noun Old English, from Latin pinus, reinforced in Middle English by Old French pin."
pine.mechanism_sentence: pine 是拉丁语 pinus 借进来的：古英语本有自己的词 furh（今天 fir 的老祖宗），借词后来居上，成了「松树」的正名；pinus 再往深处追，或许与它饱含的树脂（肥、胀）有关——这一步来源只作推测。

semantic_path.how: 借词打败本地词：古英语本来用 furh 指这类针叶树，pinus 经古法语与直接借入两路进入英语，逐渐占下『松树』的正名，furh 退守 fir 一词——词库今义即借词这一支。
